data.title: Claim on an existing branch leaves a conflicted merge and reports success

data.text:
Claim on an existing branch leaves a conflicted merge and reports success
Second instance: claiming LS-worker-lane-override (branch 12673 commits behind main) left the new worktree mid-merge with an UD path on the split ddflow/services/adopt.py; claim answered how=created with no warning. Source: infra/worktree/_create.py ignores the GitResult of sync(wt, cfg).

chunk_findings.detail: The previous LOW still holds. The `parse_lane_tiers` change now rejects case-variant duplicates in the current spec, but it does not update `write_lanes`' orphan check, which compares existing lane file names case-sensitively. On a case-insensitive, case-preserving filesystem (macOS/Windows defaults), changing `mcp.lane_tools = "IMPL=all"` to `mcp.lane_tools = "impl=all"` leaves `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-IMPL.json` not recognized as the existing file for lane `impl`, so adopt misreports or rewrites the same file instead of treating it as current.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:write_lanes

chunk_findings.detail: `_LANE_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*")` requires the first character to be alphanumeric, but the adjacent comment says only a leading dot is forbidden and the knob doc says a lane name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`. For example, `mcp.lane_tools = "_impl=all"` or `"-impl=all"` raises `ValueError` even though both are valid according to the stated allowed characters and would produce valid file names. If leading `_` and `-` are actually meant to be invalid, the comment/doc are wrong; otherwise the regex should allow either as the first character.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/mcp.py:26

chunk_findings.detail: `wide` is sorted lexicographically by lane name (`sorted(lane for lane, tier in lanes.items() if deferral_note(env, tier=tier))`), but then the returned note uses `deferral_note(env, tier=lanes[wide[0]])`. The docstring says the note should be "for the widest" deferral, yet the widest is not the alphabetically first lane. For example, with `[mcp].lane_tools = "alpha=narrow_defer, zeta=wide_defer"` and no note for `[mcp].worker_tools`, both tiers produce non-empty deferral notes where `wide_defer` is the wider of the two; the code returns `alpha`'s narrower note because `"alpha" < "zeta"`, while labeling it as applying to both lanes. The returned doctor note then understates the actual widest deferral.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:doctor_notes

chunk_findings.detail: This test creates a hard link named `worker-mcp-alias.json` to the current `worker-mcp-impl.json` and asserts that `alias` is not reported as “no longer in”. A hard link is a distinct directory entry with a distinct lane name, not the case-insensitive-filesystem collision the test claims to model. An unconfigured `alias` lane file is a real stale lane file and should be reported, just like `old` later in the same test. If `write_lanes` honors this assertion, it suppresses valid stale-lane warnings for any extra hard-linked lane name; conversely, the test still would not catch the original case-only macOS/Windows issue.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_a_lane_file_that_is_another_name_for_a_current_one_is_not_reported_stale

chunk_findings.detail: The test saves the exit code as `_code` but never asserts `_code != 0`. An implementation (or CLI wrapper) that catches the bad `lane_tools` value, prints `impl=bogus` without a traceback, and still exits 0 and proceeds with `adopt` would satisfy the assertion, contradicting the test’s stated “stops adopt” purpose.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_a_hand_edited_bad_lane_list_stops_adopt_with_the_reason_not_a_traceback

chunk_findings.detail: `wide` is sorted by lane name (`sorted(lane for lane, tier in lanes.items() if deferral_note(env, tier=tier))`), but the note text is then taken from `lanes[wide[0]]`, the alphabetically first lane. The docstring says the lane note should be “one note for the widest.” With a spec such as `[mcp].lane_tools = "beta=core\nalpha=auto"` where `auto` is the wider tier and its `deferral_note` text differs, this returns the `core` note for `alpha` and appends both lane names to that narrower note. The selection should order by tier width, not lane name.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:doctor_notes

chunk_findings.detail: The new final case asserts only that the single note contains "`all` tool tier" for `_cfg(worker="all", lanes="rev=all")`. A `doctor_notes` implementation that, when `worker_tools == "all"`, emits one generic all-tier note and then ignores the per-lane override would satisfy this assertion even though the lane `rev` is never reported—the exact regression this test is meant to prevent. The preceding lane-only case does require `"rev"` in the note, showing that the overlap case should likewise assert that the affected lane is named.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_the_doctor_counts_a_lane_on_the_whole_tool_list

chunk_findings.detail: The new stale-file check uses `lane.casefold() not in named`, which treats lane names as case-insensitive regardless of the filesystem. On a case-sensitive filesystem (Linux default), a leftover `worker-mcp-IMPL.json` is a distinct file from the configured `worker-mcp-impl.json`, but `IMPL.casefold()` equals `"impl"`, so it is skipped and never reported as “no longer in [mcp].lane_tools”. Concrete input: repo contains `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-IMPL.json` and `[mcp].lane_tools = "impl=all"`; `write_lanes` writes `worker-mcp-impl.json`, sees the uppercase file, and suppresses the stale-lane warning even though that uppercase file remains orphaned. The previous `samefile` check handled this correctly; the replacement should consult the real filesystem case rules, for example `os.path.normcase`/`samefile`, not unconditional `casefold`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:write_lanes

chunk_findings.detail: On a case-sensitive filesystem, a case-only lane rename silently leaves an extra lane config unreported. With an existing `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-rev.json` and spec `Rev=all`, the function writes `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-Rev.json`; `named` contains `rev.casefold()`, so the old distinct file is skipped and no "no longer in [mcp].lane_tools" note is appended, whereas the old `samefile` check would have reported it. This means two per-lane files for the same logical lane remain without the promised stale-file note.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:write_lanes

chunk_findings.detail: The new overlap assertion `assert "`all` tool tier" in note and "rev" in note` still does not prove the per-lane override `rev=all` is reported as `all` when `worker_tools="all"`. Given that input, an implementation returning `"worker `all` tool tier; lane `rev` uses `standard` tool tier"` would satisfy the assertion while misreporting the lane tier, because the `all` tier substring could come from the worker note and the earlier lane-only case does not exercise this overlap branch. The test added by the previous fix remains too weak to catch a bug where the worker-level `all` overwrites the per-lane value.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_the_doctor_counts_a_lane_on_the_whole_tool_list

chunk_findings.detail: Replacing `samefile` with `lane.casefold() not in named` treats a different inode as the live lane file. On a case-sensitive filesystem, with `[mcp].lane_tools` `review=core` and an existing `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-Review.json` whose `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` is still `all`, `write_lanes` writes `worker-mcp-review.json` at `core` and emits no "no longer in [mcp].lane_tools (left in place)" line, because `"Review".casefold()` is in `named`. The leftover file is not the one just written and keeps the old tier; the old check only suppressed that note when the paths were the same file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:write_lanes

chunk_findings.detail: `samefile` is used to decide whether a spelling difference is just a case-insensitive filesystem alias, but it returns True for any two path names that resolve to the same inode. On a case-sensitive filesystem, a distinct directory entry whose name differs only in case from a configured lane can be a hard link (or symlink) to the current lane file: for `[mcp].lane_tools = "impl=all"` and a Linux hard link named `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-IMPL.json` pointing to `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-impl.json`, `_is_current("IMPL", {"impl": "all"})` returns True via `samefile`, so `write_lanes` suppresses the “worker-mcp-IMPL.json is no longer in [mcp].lane_tools” note even though the `IMPL` entry is a separate directory entry no longer named in the spec. The check should distinguish the actual directory entries when names differ on a case-sensitive filesystem, not infer case-insensitivity from inode identity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:_is_current

chunk_findings.detail: The test first calls `WM.write_lanes(tmp_path, {"command": "c"}, "impl=all")`, which creates `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-impl.json`, then unconditionally runs `(tmp_path / WM.lane_rel("IMPL")).symlink_to(tmp_path / "missing.json")`. On a case-insensitive, case-preserving filesystem (default APFS on macOS and NTFS on Windows), `worker-mcp-IMPL.json` and `worker-mcp-impl.json` are the same path, so the just-created file already exists there; `Path.symlink_to` raises `FileExistsError` instead of creating the dangling symlink. The neighboring case-sensitivity test explicitly skips when the filesystem ignores case, so this test fails on default macOS/Windows test runs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_a_dangling_symlink_spelled_like_a_lane_is_reported_not_a_crash

chunk_findings.detail: On a case-sensitive filesystem, a second directory entry whose name only differs by case is still not current, but `_is_current` treats `Path.samefile` as identity. After `write_lanes` writes `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-impl.json` for `impl=all`, a hard link or a live symlink named `worker-mcp-IMPL.json` pointing at that file casefold-matches `impl` and `samefile` returns True, so the `IMPL` name is omitted from the "no longer in [mcp].lane_tools" notes. The dangling-symlink path is the only case-variant extra that is reported; a resolvable alias is silently kept, which contradicts the docstring that a second file where case counts is not current (and the hard-link test for a non-casefold name).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:_is_current

chunk_findings.detail: On a case-sensitive filesystem, `_is_current` reports a hard-linked lane file as current when its name differs only in case from a live lane. For example, with `[mcp].lane_tools = "review=core"` and existing files `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-review.json` plus `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-Review.json` hard-linked to it, `write_lanes` writes the lowercase file and then iterates both names. For `listed="Review"`, the casefold match with `"review"` is found and `samefile` returns `True` because the two paths share an inode, so `_is_current` returns `True` and no "no longer in [mcp].lane_tools (left in place)" note is emitted. This contradicts the function's own docstring ("Where case counts that is a second file, which keeps its old tier and is not current"): on a case-sensitive filesystem the two names are distinct directory entries, and only on a case-insensitive filesystem should their identities be collapsed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:_is_current

chunk_findings.detail: On a case-insensitive filesystem (default macOS APFS, Windows NTFS), after `write_lanes` writes `worker-mcp-impl.json`, the next line tries to create a symlink at `worker-mcp-IMPL.json`. Because the filesystem resolves the two spellings to the same path, `Path.symlink_to` raises `FileExistsError` before the assertion is reached. The test needs the same `pytest.skip` guard that `test_a_second_file_that_differs_only_in_case_keeps_its_old_tier_and_is_reported` uses when `(tmp_path / WM.lane_rel("IMPL")).exists()` after writing the lower-case lane.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_a_dangling_symlink_spelled_like_a_lane_is_reported_not_a_crash

chunk_findings.detail: A stale case-variant lane file that is a hard link to the current file is silently treated as current. On a case-sensitive filesystem with `[mcp].lane_tools` `review=core`, if an existing `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-Review.json` is hard-linked to `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-review.json`, `write_lanes` writes the `review` file, then `_is_current("Review", {"review": "core"})` reaches the `casefold()` match and calls `(repo / lane_rel("Review")).samefile(repo / lane_rel("review"))`; since the two directory entries share an inode, `samefile` returns `True`, so no `worker-mcp-Review.json is no longer in [mcp].lane_tools (left in place)` note is appended. `Review.json` is still a separate file name the spec does not name and is left in place, contradicting the function's documented “where case counts that is a second file … is not current” behavior and the new hard-link test’s expectation that an un-named lane is reported even as a hard link to a current one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:_is_current

chunk_findings.detail: On a case-insensitive filesystem (default macOS APFS or Windows), the first `WM.write_lanes(tmp_path, {"command": "c"}, "impl=all")` creates `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-impl.json`. The next line, `(tmp_path / WM.lane_rel("IMPL")).symlink_to(tmp_path / "missing.json")`, then resolves to the same directory entry as that already-existing file. `Path.symlink_to` does not overwrite an existing path; it raises `FileExistsError`, so the test fails before reaching its assertion. The adjacent new case-only test explicitly skips on such filesystems, but this one has no equivalent guard, so the test suite breaks on those platforms.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_a_dangling_symlink_spelled_like_a_lane_is_reported_not_a_crash

chunk_findings.detail: On a case-insensitive volume, `write_lanes(..., "impl=all")` already creates `lane_rel("impl")`, which is the same directory entry as `lane_rel("IMPL")`. The next line, `(tmp_path / WM.lane_rel("IMPL")).symlink_to(...)`, raises `FileExistsError` before `_stale` runs, so the test errors instead of asserting the dangling case-variant note. The neighboring case-only test skips when `lane_rel("review")` already exists; this one does not, so the added case fails on APFS/default macOS tmp dirs.
